sources.entry: Lazy - Keyboard-driven commands to manage your surroundings directly from your mac.

summary.name: Lazy
summary.one_liner: Lazy is a keyboard-driven Mac app that lets you trigger actions to control your surroundings, connected devices, and online services via a shortcut and typed command.
use_cases: Turn on lights or smart plugs without leaving the keyboard
Trigger IFTTT applets and Zapier zaps from the Mac
Start a Netlify site deploy with a shortcut
Control a robot vacuum or coffee machine from the desktop
Send an SMS or Slack message via a shortcut
Keep focus by running actions without switching apps
summary.what_it_does: Lazy runs on the Mac and lets you press ⌥ + ⌘ + K, then type the name of an action to run it. Actions can be created by pasting a webhook URL into Lazy and assigning a keyboard shortcut to it. The page describes connecting devices and services such as smart plugs, bulbs, robot vacuums, security systems, Spotify, Slack, and Netlify. It also says Lazy can trigger IFTTT applets and Zapier Zaps, which it describes as giving access to 1000+ devices and services. The page is mostly promotional and gives few technical details about setup or internals.
notable: Global shortcut ⌥ + ⌘ + K opens a typed command palette for actions
Webhook-based actions: paste a webhook URL and assign a shortcut
Integrates with IFTTT and Zapier for 1000+ devices and services
caveats: Page does not state pricing or whether it is free, paid, or open source
Device and service support depends on webhooks and IFTTT/Zapier integrations, not direct control of every device
